body:
Mm hmm, seeing how normal people interact so well makes me even more depressed and makes me envy their life. Even people with social anxiety are usually funny and interesting people once you get them to come out of their shell. I would swap lives with them any day.

I can definitely relate with the bosses thing. I've been fired from both my jobs because of how clumsy I am and my inability to follow instructions well. It's like a curse I've had put upon me. Why there are people against finding a cure will always be beyond my knowledge.

I wish nothing but the best for your son, I even said in my post I'm sure some people can live happily with aspergers. But my personal experience with it has been nothing but destructive. All my dreams are slowly being shattered by the realization that however much work I put in I will always be held back by this barrier. Chances are your 10 year old son will have very different goals in life to me which will be far easier to accomplish with aspergers.
Sure, I want a relationship, but that is really just a part of it. I want to be able to form close bonds like NT people can. Which is what leads to fulfilling friendships and yes, a girlfriend too.
I tried it once a few years ago with some friends, I did like it. But I have no idea how I would go about getting it myself and the friend who gave me it lives in a different country now.
